The disk filled up and took the api down with it: a `report-export` job wrote 40 CSV parts of 512 MB each (about 20 GB) into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports` between 03:05:00 and 03:12:48.

The disk warning hit 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 Postgres failed with "could not extend file … No space left on device", the api aborted its transaction and shut down its worker pool, and at 03:14:06 it exited with status 1.

It never came back. The proxy logged "upstream api refused connection" every two minutes from 03:16:00 through 03:28:00 at the end of the log (67 times), and there is not a single api line after the exit. Web and proxy kept serving 200s throughout.

The cache "slow command" warnings are unrelated noise; they run at the same steady rate from the first line of the log.

To recover, clear the export parts off that volume and start the api again. To prevent a repeat, the export job needs a size cap or its own volume.

The log's timestamps are all 2026-03-09, 02:00 to 05:30, so if the outage you mean was last night, this file is not the current one.
